Hi Anya — thanks, glad the demo helped. Quick note to confirm we received your usage profile and requirements. I put together a short sketch attached (Redwood_VPC_SLA_Skus.pdf) and a quick rationale below — this is to help you decide which pricing axis aligns with your goals.

Summary (short):
- Seat-based (capacity unit) is easier for predictable throughput and when you want to lock a hardware+support bundle; it aligns to Reserved pools and gives predictable p95 latency targets. Good if you value predictable monthly spend and want an SLA-backed throughput guarantee.
- Metered (usage) is lower upfront and better when monthly volume is variable or when optimizing for cost per inference; cost scales with tokens or GPU-hours. Good for bursty workloads or short-term projects.

Platform fee: applied as a % uplift on top of capacity or metered consumption for Private (VPC/on-prem) — covers control plane, SSO/KMS integrations, audit logs, and quarterly security reviews. For multi-year commitments we typically amortize the platform fee into an effective lower monthly platform surcharge (example in the attached).

Assumptions that shift the recommendation:
- If your bursts are frequent and sustained (>20% of days) metered + burst pool is cheaper.
- If you need strict latency SLO and dedicated GPU pools, seat-based Reserved capacity reduces tail latency and billing uncertainty.
- Compliance-heavy engagements often prefer Reserved + higher support tier (24x7) so Redwood can commit to runbooks and quarterly reviews.

Hi Anya — looping in some worked numbers below (high-level; see attached spreadsheet for line-by-line). Happy to refine after you review.

Worked example assumptions (quick):
- Baseline: 6,000,000 requests/mo × 350 tokens/request = 2.1B tokens/mo.
- Seat-based reserved: we size by GPUs; for your profile we estimate 6 reserved capacity units (RCUs) to hit baseline p50 with ~1.5x headroom; reserved unit = capacity for ~1M requests/mo at seq=350 with p50 latency target.
- Metered: price per 1M tokens = $A (see sheet). Burst pool is available as an overage metered bucket at 1.25× the standard metered rate; customers can configure a burst reserve that charges only when used.

High-level numbers (rounded monthly):
- Seat-based reserved (6 RCUs) + Standard platform fee (12% amortized at 36 months) + Premium support upgrade = ~$78k / month (effective $0.013 / inference at p50, $0.020 at p95 including platform & support amortized).
- Metered (no reserved capacity) with burst reserve + Premium support = ~$64k / month (effective $0.010 / inference p50, $0.018 at p95).

Notes:
- Metered wins on baseline cost because you don't pre-pay for unused capacity, but sustained bursts will push metered above reserved.
- Reserved secures predictable p95 latency and gives lower tail-latency variance.
- Platform fee amortization assumes a 36-month commit; for 12-months the platform fee uplift is higher (~+3–4% on top of the per-month numbers).

Discount ladder (illustrative):
- 12-month commit: no platform fee reduction; small volume discount (5%);
- 24-month commit: platform fee reduced by 20% (on the platform portion) + 8% volume;
- 36-month commit: platform fee reduced by 35% (on the platform portion) + 12% volume.

I'll attach the spreadsheet with the cell-level calc. If you'd like, we can provision a temporary 30-day Reserved pilot at a reduced rate to gather p95 data against your workloads before signing.
